REPORT
Date October 8, 19 40.
Subject Transportation Coolies on Customs Jetty, Pontoons Nos 6 and 7 -
Mediation by Municipal Police -further report. - Dispute settled.
Made by D. I. Kao Ven Ken Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

On October 3, it was ascertained from the
Customs foreman that he had no objection to the Police
suggestion of mediation and would accept same with
the approval of the Customs authorities. It was then
arranged that he meet the Police and Customs representa-
tives at the Customs House at 10 a.m. October 4.
At 10 a.m. October 4, D.S.I. Wright and D.I.
Kao had an interview with Mr. C.H. Davis, Tidesurveyor,
at his office in the Customs House. The Customs fore-
man was also present. The Police suggestion was again
discussed. The Customs foreman with the assistance
of a Chinese 2nd class tidesurveyor named Van insisted
that the Customs foreman collect transportation charges
from the shipping hongs direct and pay the coolies
through their foremen instead of the present system
whereby the coolie foremen collect the money from
the shipping hongs direct. At this juncture, it was
again explained to them that it has been a custom
that shipping hongs have good relations with the
coolie foremen and entrust them not only with the
transportation but also the protection of the cargo.
In case of theft, the coolie foremen have to compensate
the shipping hongs for the loss, and as a matter of
fact the shipping hongs regard them almost as their
regular employees. It is also to be noted that this
dispute between the Customs foreman and the coolie
foremen arose from the intention of the Customs foreman
to collect $0.30 from the shipping hongs per large box

日期：1940年10月8日。
主题：海关码头第6号和第7号浮桥上的搬运苦力——
工部局警务处调解——进一步报告。——纠纷已解决。
呈报人：督察高仁肯 (D. I. Kao Ven Ken) 转呈人：督察克劳福德 (D. I. Crawford)

10月3日，从海关工头处获悉，他对警方提出的调解建议不持异议，并在获得海关当局批准后予以接受。随后安排他于10月4日上午10时在海关大楼与警方及海关代表会面。
10月4日上午10时，副督察赖特 (D.S.I. Wright) 和督察高 (D.I. Kao) 在海关大楼的办公室会见了验潮员 C.H. Davis 先生。海关工头也在场。再次讨论了警方的建议。海关工头在一位名为 Van 的华籍二等验潮员的协助下，坚持要求由海关工头直接向航运商号收取运输费，并通过苦力工头支付给苦力，以取代目前由苦力工头直接向航运商号收款的现行制度。在此关头，再次向他们解释，航运商号与苦力工头保持良好关系是一种惯例，不仅将运输任务委托给他们，还将货物保护工作委托给他们。一旦发生盗窃，苦力工头必须向航运商号赔偿损失，事实上，航运商号几乎将他们视为正式雇员。还值得注意的是，海关工头与苦力工头之间的这场纠纷，源于海关工头意图向航运商号就每个大箱子收取0.30美元

instead of $0.20 as hitherto and pay the coolies only
half of the earnings.
Finally Mr. C.H. Davis reached a decision
whereby the Customs foreman work in the Examination
Shed with full power, while in order to avoid throwing
the 200 casual coolies out of employment the Customs
authorities would shut their eyes to their transporting
cargo through the Customs Jetty to the lighters via
a bridge between Pontoon No.7 and the Customs Examination
Shed, and the Customs foreman has nothing to do with
them. Thereupon D.S.I. Wright and D. I. Kao accompanied
by 2nd Class Tidesurveyor Van and the Customs foreman
visited the said bridge and confirmed the locations.
It was then arranged with Van and the Customs foreman
that the Customs foreman should meet the casual coolie
foremen at Police Headquarters at 2 p.m. October 7
so that the terms of settlement be made known to both
parties, and a compromise be confirmed.
At 2 p.m. October 7, Chang Ah-nyi(張阿二),
representing the casual coolie foremen and coolies
attended Police Headquarters, but the Customs foreman
failed to turn up. At 4 p.m. the same day, the result
of mediation was explained to him and finally he
accepted the terms for settlement.
It is to be noted that it is the third time the
Customs foreman failed to keep his word to attend
conferences. As the terms of settlement were announced

最终，C.H. Davis 先生作出决定，海关工头在查验棚内拥有全权开展工作，同时为了避免使200名临时苦力失业，海关当局将对他们通过第7号浮桥与海关查验棚之间的一座桥梁，经海关码头将货物运至驳船的行为视而不见，且海关工头与他们无关。随后，副督察赖特和督察高在二等验潮员 Van 和海关工头的陪同下，视察了上述桥梁并确认了位置。
随后与 Van 及海关工头商定，海关工头应于10月7日下午2时在警察总局会见临时苦力工头，以便向双方通报和解条款，并确认妥协方案。
10月7日下午2时，代表临时苦力工头和苦力的张阿二 (Chang Ah-nyi) 出席了警察总局，但海关工头未露面。当日下午4时，向他解释了调解结果，最终他接受了和解条款。
值得注意的是，这已是海关工头第三次未能信守诺言出席会议。鉴于和解条款已由

REPORT
Date October 1, 1940.

（印：REGISTRY File No. 378）

Subject Transportation Coolies on Customs Jetty, Pontoons Nos. 6 and 7 -
Mediation by Municipal Police - further report.

Made by D.I. Kao Yen Ken Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

In view of the fact that the Customs foreman
failed to attend mediation on September 20, Mr. C.H.
Davis, Tidesurveyor, was interviewed at the Customs
House on September 23 and facts of the case laid
before him. Mr. Davis promised to instruct the
foreman to call on the Police the following day.
On September 24, the Customs foreman together
with three of his partners named Eu Tsoo-un(欧祖男),
residing at 232 Yien Ching Li, Amoy Road, Kan Loong-
siu (干龍水), residing at 117 Teh An Li, North Shanse
Road, and Jao Yung-chiang(喬榮姜), residing at 39
Washington Li, Kashing Road, attended Police Headquarters.
The foremen of the casual coolies were also present.
Efforts at mediation with a view to reaching a
settlement were made but agreement was not reached.
When the suggested plan for a settlement was fully
explained to the Customs foreman and his partners
and the fact pointed out that it would satisfy both
the Customs authorities and the foreman from the view-
point of control and finance while avoiding the throw-
ing out of employment of 200 coolies who are bound to
make trouble if rendered unemployed. The Customs
foreman and his partners could raise no objections
and promised to consult the other 26 partners in
respect of the percentage of money to be collected by
the Customs Foreman. It was then arranged that a
further meeting be held at Police Headquarters at
2 p.m. September 25.

日期：1940年10月1日。

（手写批注：1940年10月9日 / 警署）

主题：海关码头第6号和第7号浮桥上的搬运苦力——
工部局警务处调解——进一步报告。

呈报人：督察高仁肯 (D.I. Kao Yen Ken) 转呈人：督察克劳福德 (D. I. Crawford)。

鉴于海关工头未能出席9月20日的调解，9月23日在海关大楼会见了验潮员 C.H. Davis 先生，并向他陈述了案情事实。Davis 先生答应指示工头于次日拜访警方。
9月24日，海关工头与其三位合伙人欧祖男 (Eu Tsoo-un)，住厦门路延庆里232号；干龍水 (Kan Loong-siu)，住山西北路德安里117号；以及乔荣姜 (Jao Yung-chiang)，住嘉兴路华盛里39号，一同前往警察总局。临时苦力工头也在场。
为达成和解进行了调解努力，但未达成协议。当向海关工头及其合伙人充分解释建议的和解方案，并指出该方案从管理和财务角度来看既能满足海关当局和工头的要求，又能避免200名一旦失业必将惹是生非的苦力失去工作时，海关工头及其合伙人提不出任何反对意见，并承诺就海关工头收取款项的比例问题与其他26位合伙人协商。随后商定于9月25日下午2时在警察总局举行进一步会议。

At the appointed time on September 25, the
Customs foreman failed to attend. Late in the
afternoon he rang up and stated that he could not reach
a decision in the matter and would leave it to the
Customs authorities to decide. He promised to inform
the Police of the decision in the course of a few days.
Up to 3 p.m. September 30, no reply was forthcoming.
In view of the procrastinating attitude of the Customs
foreman, D.S.I. Wright and D.I. Kao interviewed Mr. H.E.
Olsen, Deputy Commissioner, at 3.30 p.m., September 30,
in the absence of Mr. C. H. Davis, Tidesurveyor.
Mr. Olsen stated that he was unable to reach a
decision in the matter as he was due to leave Shanghai
in the near future and suggested that the matter might
be referred to the Commissioner of Customs in writing.

9月25日约定时间，海关工头未出席。傍晚时分他打来电话，称此事无法做出决定，将留给海关当局决定。他承诺在几天内将决定通知警方。
截至9月30日下午3时，仍未收到回复。鉴于海关工头的拖延态度，在验潮员 C. H. Davis 先生缺席的情况下，副督察赖特和督察高于9月30日下午3时30分会见了副税务司 H.E. Olsen 先生。
Olsen 先生表示，由于他即将在近期离开上海，因此无法就此事项做出决定，并建议将此事项以书面形式呈报海关税务司。

REPORT

Date September 21st 1940

Subject Transportation Coolies on Customs Jetty, Pontoons Nos. 6 and 7 -
Mediation by Municipal Police - further report.
Made by D.I. Kao Yen Ken Forwarded by D. S. I. Logan.

With reference to the mediation undertaken
by the Special Branch in connection with the dispute
among transportation coolies on Customs Jetty, Pontoons
Nos. 6 and 7, no negotiations were conducted on Septem-
ber 14, as the Customs authorities had not completed
their study of the matter.

At 2.30 p.m. September 19, Mr. C. E. Davis,
~~Assistant~~ Tidesurveyor, Tidesurveyors' ~~Office~~ Office,
was interviewed. He stated that Yao Ding Fong (姚廷芳),
was officially recognized by the Customs Authorities as
the coolie foreman, and that only his men would be
allowed to work in the Customs property. Discussion
then took place as to the manner in which the cargo
outside the Customs shed would be dealt with which, up
to now, has been handled by the 200 casual coolies.
The Customs foreman suggested that the casual coolies
should be responsible for the transportation outside
the Customs shed and that as soon as the cargo arrives
at the entrance of the Shed, the transportation be
undertaken by the Customs coolies. It will be noted that
this system would not only increase the cost to the
property owners by having to pay two transportation
charges, but would cause very much inconvenience at the
Shed entrance should there be a lot of cargo. Mr. Davis
also agreed that the system suggested was impractical.

The Custom Foreman has only thirty coolies
who hitherto transported examined cargo: and, in order

日期：1940年9月21日

主题：海关码头第6号和第7号浮桥上的搬运苦力——
工部局警务处调解——进一步报告。
呈报人：督察高仁肯 (D.I. Kao Yen Ken) 转呈人：副督察洛根 (D. S. I. Logan)。

关于特别支部就海关码头第6号和第7号浮桥搬运苦力纠纷进行的调解，由于海关当局尚未完成对此事的研究，9月14日未进行谈判。

9月19日下午2时30分，会见了验潮员办公室的验潮员 C. E. Davis 先生（原文划去“助理”），（原文划去“办公室”）。他表示，姚廷芳 (Yao Ding Fong) 已获海关当局正式承认为苦力工头，且只允许其手下在海关辖地内工作。随后讨论了如何处理目前由200名临时苦力负责的、海关棚外货物的方式。海关工头建议，临时苦力应负责海关棚外的运输，一旦货物到达棚口，运输工作即由海关苦力承担。值得注意的是，这一制度不仅因需支付两笔运输费而增加货主的成本，而且如果货物量大，会在棚口造成极大不便。Davis 先生也同意所建议的制度不切实际。

海关工头仅有三十名苦力，此前一直负责运输已查验货物：并且，为了

Mr. Davis had no objection to the suggestion as he was

At 3.30 p.m. September 19, representatives
of both parties were informed of the suggestion. After
persuasion, the foremen of the casual coolies agreed,
but the Customs Foreman insisted that the transportation
charges be collected by him instead of by the foremen
as hitherto. It will also be noted that it has been
the Custom that shipping hongs have good relations with
the foremen and entrust them with the transportation as
well as the protection of the cargo. The shipping hongs
are satisfied with the foremen whom they regard almost
as their regular employees. Now, the question over the
transportation charges arose. The Customs Foreman was
asked what he intended to give the coolies and what he
expected from the cargo owners. He replied that he
would give $0.15 to the coolies but made no mention
about what he was going to charge the cargo owners.

9月19日下午3时30分，双方代表获悉了该建议。经劝说，临时苦力工头表示同意，但海关工头坚持由他而不是像以往那样由工头收取运输费。还须注意，航运商号与工头关系良好，并将货物的运输及保护工作委托给工头，这已成惯例。航运商号对工头感到满意，几乎将其视为自己的正式雇员。现在，关于运输费的问题出现了。有人询问海关工头打算付给苦力多少钱，以及期望从货主那里收取多少钱。他回答说将付给苦力0.15元，但未提及打算向货主收取多少费用。

It was apparently still his intention to charge $0.30
instead of the present rate of $0.20 which is satis-

local shipping hongs will oppose the increased rate.
It was then explained to him that if the suggested
system is approved he will get his share, the rate of
which can be reasonably talked over. He was unable
to raise any reason for opposition to the new suggestion.
Finally, he stated that he had to consult his 30
partners on the matter. He promised that five delegates
of his company would be present at Police Headquarters
to continue the mediation, at 2 p.m. September 20.

to be transported from the Bund outside the Customs Shed,

Subject Transportation Coolies operating on Customs Jetty, Pontoons
Nos. 6 and 7 - "Tai-kung" strike - Mediation by Municipal Police.

Made by D.I. Kao Yen Ken Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

（左侧手写批注：
Sent, 14/9.
FILE
1-4
）

Approximately 200 casual coolies operating on
the Customs Jetty, Pontoons Nos. 6 and 7, declared a
"tai-kung" strike at 8 a.m., September 12. They were
opposing the attempt of one Yao Ding-fong (姚廷芳),
a foreman of the Chinese Maritime Customs at the
Cargo Examination Office, to monopolize the
transportation of goods.

Representatives of the disputing parties as
follows attended Central Station, from where they
were referred to Special Branch for mediation.

Customs foreman
Yao Ding-fong (姚廷芳), alias Siao Ah-too
(小阿土), 110 Chekiang Road.

Foremen of casual coolies
Woo Ah-sai (符阿二), 26 Fan Shun Li, Ward Rd.
Chang Ah-nyi (张阿二), - do -

Yao Ding-fong, the Customs foreman, claimed
that he was authorized by the Customs Authorities
to handle transportation of all cargo on the Customs
Jetty. The authorized charge for carrying each large
box of cargo is $0.30. He claimed that he had
thirty regular coolies helping in the transportation
of cargo in the course of examination by Customs
officials and, in this connection, he decided to
pay $0.15 to the casual coolies while he retained
$0.15 for himself.

The foremen of casual coolies, however, claimed
that the Customs foreman and his men were only con-
cerned in the handling of cargo while same is being
examined. Only five per cent of cargo is examined; in
other words, the Customs foreman handled 5% of the
cargo, while the remaining 95% is carried by the
casual coolies. All the cargo has to pass through
the Customs Jetty. The local shipping hongs paid
transportation charges of the 5% of the cargo to be
examined, to the Customs foreman, at $0.30 per box.
Out of this sum, the Customs foreman gave $0.15 to
the casual coolie responsible for the transportation
of the cargo from the shore through the Customs
Examination Shed to the boats in the Whangpo River.
He kept the other $0.15 for his own coolies assisting
in the transportation while the cargo was being
examined. The foremen continued to say that
payment for the remaining 95% of the cargo was
arranged between the shipping hongs and the casual
coolie foremen direct. The charge was formerly
$0.18 or $0.20 per box and was paid direct to the
casual coolie foremen. They state that the Customs
foreman now claims that all cargo irrespective of
whether it is examined or non-examined cargo, should
be handled by him at a fixed rate of $0.30 per box,
out of which the casual coolies were to get only
$0.15. They also stated that the coolies were

opposing the monopoly attempt and insisting that
the old system be adhered to. They also mentioned
that shipping hongs were also opposing the increased
charge on non-examined cargo.
As the matter was complicated and it was
necessary to secure the views of the Customs
Authorities, representatives of the both parties
were instructed that work be resumed on the old
system pending mediation by the Special Branch. It
was meanwhile arranged for them to attend Special
Branch at 2 p.m. September 13.
As arranged, work was resumed at 5.30 p.m.
September 13.
At 11.30 a.m. September 13, Mr. G.W. Davis,
Assistant Tidesurveyor, Tidesurveyors' General Office,
was interviewed. He was informed of the case. He
stated that the Customs Authorities recently published
a notice authorizing a uniform charge of $0.30 per
large box. He stated that the notice was published
at the instance of the Customs foreman who made a
petition on behalf of the coolies on the plea of the
high cost of living. He did not know that the
foreman wanted to keep half of the $0.30 on the
non-examined cargo for himself. He promised to
investigate the matter and inform D.I. Kao Yen-ken
at 10 a.m. September 14.
